newsitem.title: FRANCE: Analyst ups French '96 wheat, barley crop estimate.
newsitem.headline: Analyst ups French '96 wheat, barley crop estimate.

text.p: French grains analyst Strategie Grains said on Monday it was revising upwards its estimate for French 1996 soft wheat and barley output, citing better than expected yields in northern and eastern France.

The Paris-based analyst raised its forecast for the national soft wheat crop to between 33.3 and 33.7 million tonnes from a mid-August forecast of 32.05 million tonnes and from 29.9 million tonnes produced in 1995.
Total spring and winter barley output was revised up to 9.4 million tonnes from 8.5 million tonnes forecast on August 15 and from 7.7 million tonnes produced in 1995.

Strategie Grains said the new forecast took into account the "better than expected" performance of crops in northern and eastern France after initial fears of yield loss due to prolonged dryness in the spring.
The analyst explained that when the August 15 prediction was released, combining was just starting in these regions.
The new estimate includes reports from local farmers and grain industry sources in the two regions, where harvesting is now completed.
"The new forecast is based on extremely favourable weather conditions in late June and early July," the analyst told Reuters.
Prolonged dryness in the spring had raised concern over yield loss in northern France but scattered showers and good cloud cover helped improve growing conditions, she said.
The new wheat crop estimate assumes an average national yield of between 6.98 and 7.07 tonnes per hectare against 6.71 tonnes predicted in mid-August and 6.61 last year.
Total wheat area is expected to grow to 4.77 million hectares from 4.51 million ha.
In northern France farmers are reporting record yields of over 10 tonnes per hectare on some patches and Strategie grains is putting the average yield for the region at over nine tonnes.
The centre France wheat belt and the Burgundy region, two areas that suffered most from the a moisture shortage, are reporting yields as low as 6.2-6.3 tonnes and 5.8-6.0 tonnes, respectively.
Strategie Grains also revised upwards its estimate for the national barley yield to 6.2 tonnes from 5.8 tonnes in mid-August and from 5.54 tonnes last year.
Total barley area should reach 1.52 million hectares against 1.39 million in 1995.
In mid-August France's farm ministry raised its forecast for the wheat crop to 31.3 million tonnes from a previous target of 30.5 million tonnes.
But market sources said the estimate could be revised again when the ministry releases new crop data in mid-September.
France's grain office ONIC is expected to provide its first post-harvest estimate for the 1996 crop when it releases its monthly market report next week.
ONIC predicted on July 10 - before harvest got under way - a soft wheat crop of 30.9 million tonnes and a barley crop of 7.9 million tonnes.
